main_body: Gray stone mortar bowl with a green herb filling visible in its opening and a brown pestle angled out of it
top_band: Rim and opening ellipse at rows ~7-10: light gray rim at the left and back, with a green filling ellipse (light/mid green) inside; the pestle crosses it
evidence: Reading a column through the bowl centre: the light gray back rim, then the green filling ellipse (about 3 rows) seen from above, then the lighter front rim edge. Below that is a darker gray bowl body of about 5 rows that tapers to a foot. The interior is visible as an ellipse and the front face is a separate vertical surface, so it reads as a 3/4 container and not a rim-only or flat-band drawing.

style.evidence: The outline is a dark blue-gray that leans toward the stone, not pure black. The stone ramp has only about 4 steps (rim highlight, mid, dark, deep), and the green and the brown pestle have about 3 each. The bowl body is a fairly flat gray fill with little speckle or per-stone texture. Tiles carry fewer colours than the richly textured stall and well references, so it looks thinner and flatter next to them.
